_meta.task: TASK_911 (D69) -- identity pins for load-bearing gitignored artifacts
_meta.purpose: runs/ is gitignored by design, so git's clean-tree gate cannot see these files change. A backup restore or mtime-preserving sync can silently overwrite a deployed repair with stale content (D69's forensics, 2026-08-25: runs/809_decision_rule_rescue/recompute_best.py regressed to its June revision this way, and the only in-repo detector was a red test the factory nearly deleted). This manifest pins {path, sha256, provenance, why_load_bearing} for every gitignored file a suite, gate, or launch note is known to depend on, so a divergence is a loud, checkable fact instead of an invisible one.
_meta.discovery_rule: A file belongs here iff a suite, gate, or launch note names it. Do not add speculative entries.
_meta.verifier: tools/verify_gitignored_pins.py -- import verify_all()/refuse_on_divergence() for programmatic use, or run `python -m tools.verify_gitignored_pins` for a CLI check of the whole manifest (exit 0 = all OK, 1 = at least one DIVERGED or MISSING, 2 = no DIVERGED/MISSING but at least one UNPINNED).
_meta.promote_path: Deliberate re-pin ONLY: `python -m tools.verify_gitignored_pins --promote-pin <path> --provenance '<...>' --why '<...>' --evidence '<re-derivation evidence, named>'`. Never re-pins silently; the tool refuses --promote-pin without --evidence. A divergence found by a plain verify run is a FINDING for the operator, never auto-repromoted.
_meta.sha256_null_means: the manifest names this path as load-bearing but no known-good sha256 has ever been recorded for it in this repo (it has never been seen present-and-verified from this host). Such an entry always reports MISSING or UNPINNED, never OK -- it exists so the gap itself is tracked and visible, not so it can be silently satisfied.
